title: Ramon: The Reluctant Recruit Who Became the Team to Beat
body: Ramon wasn't even sure he wanted in when the Buckaroo Football League launched in 2023, and his debut season with Araleasers looked like a man with one foot out the door: 4-10, the 6 seed, a fifth-place finish, and exactly two pickups all year. Zero trades, too. It was a quiet rookie campaign from a guy who has never been accused of being quiet about anything else.

Then 2024 happened. Araleasers went a perfectly balanced 7-7, grabbed the 3 seed, won a playoff game, and made it all the way to Buckaroo Bowl II, where Kaushal's Habibsters finished off their back-to-back and left Ramon as runner-up. It was the best finish of his career, and he did it on a single waiver pickup, the most hands-off contender run you'll ever see. The season also produced his career low, a 56.4-point dud against Kaushal in week 12, a fitting footnote for a manager who is 4-8 lifetime against Habib.

Then came 2025, the strangest chapter in league history. Ramon ran Araleasers through week 8, got kicked for inactivity, and watched his abandoned roster carry on as Ramon's Remains, opening the post-Ramon era with a 94.76-92.02 win over Alan. The team finished 5-11 and fifth, yet put up 1,523.7 points, the most of any of his seasons, and every one of those asterisked games still sits on his record. Somewhere a team without a manager was making four trades and eight pickups, which is more activity than Ramon logged in his first two seasons combined.

The 2026 comeback is the plot twist nobody ordered. Back as No Banner only HULK, Ramon opened with a 177.9-point demolition of Mekhi in week 1, the best week of his career, and has rolled to a 6-1 start with 927.4 points and a 37% shot at the title. Fittingly, Mekhi is the one manager he truly owns at 6-3 lifetime, while Sonny (5-7), Randy (4-7) and Alan (5-6) still hold the edge on him, and he's 1-0 against each of the newcomers, Zoe and Jordan. One trade and four pickups in, he's managing like someone who actually showed up this time.

So here stands Brucie: a Chicago-born Bills convert, a former league dropout, a 26-31 career record with zero Bowl titles and zero last-place finishes, and right now the best team in the league. Nothing unites the Buckaroo faithful like rooting against the guy on top, and Ramon has never given them a better target. The question for the back half of 2026 is whether the reluctant recruit finally finishes the job he almost got in 2024.
